text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT DETECTED: High reject rate on Dedicated pool eu-west-2 (pool-id: dp-eu2-11). Error type: 429/rate_limited spikes and p95 latency >1.2s. Paging eng-oncall.

oncall-elaine: seeing 5xxs + 429s across several routes, spike started ~12:03 UTC. Traffic ~3x baseline. Multiple customers reporting slow responses. Can we toggle burst and steer traffic?

sre-raj: looking at autoscaler — it reached max replicas and burst slices exhausted. I can try a manual autoscale safety switch and route non-critical traffic out.

infra-ian: prepping emergency pool (dp-eu2-emergency). Attaching nodes now — ETA ~90s.

oncall-elaine: go ahead. prefer routing + feature-shutdown over wholesale quota cuts if possible. Notify CS before throttling customer SLAs.

sre-raj: running command now:
```bash
redwoodctl pools toggle-burst --pool dp-eu2-11 --enable=false --reason "safety-switch during surge"
```
Command returned: OK. Burst disabled, autoscaler pinned to min_replicas.

infra-ian: emergency pool attach in progress...

ops-bot: Deploy event: emergency pool dp-eu2-emergency attached (4 nodes) by infra-ian

sre-raj: updating routing policy to shift low-priority traffic to emergency pool:
```json
{"route":"/v1/generate","shift":"20%","condition":"customer_tier!=enterprise"}
```
Applied.

prod-maya: suggestion: toggle off real-time reranking & non-essential post-processing for non-enterprise to cut token usage. Can disable via feature-flag quickly.

oncall-elaine: agreed — @prod-maya do it, coordinate w/CS.

prod-maya: disabled reranking for non-enterprise at 12:08 UTC.

cs-luke: ACME and two other mid-market customers reported errors. I told them we're routing non-critical jobs and may throttle non-enterprise workloads temporarily; they acknowledged.

sre-raj: metrics update: 429 rate dropping from ~18% -> ~2% within 3 minutes after routing + feature toggle. p95 latency returning to baseline. Keeping burst disabled to avoid runaway autoscale.

oncall-elaine: action plan: keep emergency pool attached for 30m, monitor GPU util and error rates. If stable, re-enable burst with a lower cap and faster cooldown.

infra-ian: set emergency pool TTL = 30m. Will detach after TTL.

ops-bot: Incident update: mitigation in place — rate spikes reduced, customers degraded but functional.

oncall-elaine: creating incident ticket and notes. Weekly follow-up: 1) root-cause analysis for traffic spike, 2) adjust default burst caps for dp-eu2-11, 3) implement early throttling heuristics on anonymous/non-SLA routes, 4) add runbook step for manual-burst-toggle.

sre-raj: collecting logs, scaler traces, and KV cache stats now and will upload to the incident doc.

cs-luke: consolidating customer comms, will send updates to impacted list with timeline and mitigation steps.

prod-maya: planning canary to re-enable reranking for a small subset after traffic normalizes.

oncall-elaine: thanks everyone. Closing pager for now — monitor for 1h, reopen if regressions. :white_check_mark:
